headline: High: OpenHands can read/write mounted files while Great Expectations consumes data files, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read files in its runtime sandbox and use MCP servers, while Great Expectations ingests data sources and writes validation results/documentation. If Great Expectations outputs are mounted into OpenHands, file content can be treated as trusted instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Great Expectations outputs are mounted into OpenHands's runtime files
IF OpenHands is configured to parse those files as task instructions or MCP payloads
mitigations: Separate the two runtimes' mounted directories
Mark Great Expectations outputs as data-only and non-executable
Add a manual review step before OpenHands consumes validation artifacts
Disable MCP ingestion for files originating from Great Expectations
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation, while OpenHands can read files in its runtime and has broad network egress. If sensitive data is placed in shared mounted files, OpenHands can transmit it to its model provider or other APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from the profiles, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF sensitive data is mounted into OpenHands's runtime
IF OpenHands sends file contents to its configured model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Keep sensitive Great Expectations inputs out of shared mounts
Use a redacted copy for OpenHands analysis
Restrict OpenHands network egress at the runtime boundary
Rotate or scope model-provider keys to non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data-class filtering

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations writes validation results and documentation, and OpenHands has write_filesystem plus modify_git_state with broad runtime access. If both operate on the same mounted workspace, they can overwrite each other's files or git state without coordination. The profiles show overlapping write surfaces and no locking mechanism, so the conflict is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted workspace
IF OpenHands modifies git state while Great Expectations writes validation artifacts
mitigations: Give each agent a separate workspace
Freeze git operations while Great Expectations runs
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Take a quick backup before shared edits
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that OpenHands can read and act on with shell, browser, and git capabilities. If OpenHands treats those outputs as authoritative, a bad validation or misread result can cascade into commits or runtime actions. The pair has a clear A-to-B handoff and OpenHands has downstream authority, so the blast radius is large.
conditions: IF OpenHands consumes Great Expectations validation output without independent verification
IF OpenHands is allowed to commit or execute follow-on actions based on that output
mitigations: Require a human review before acting on validation results
Compare results against a second check or baseline
Limit OpenHands to read-only analysis for this workflow
Log the exact source file for every acted-on assertion
requires-engineering: add verification gates before shell/git actions

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations handles data quality tests, validation results, and documentation, while OpenHands handles files in its runtime and model-provider API keys. If regulated data is placed into the runtime, OpenHands's broad egress and external model calls can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific regime, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a confirmed violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in files mounted into OpenHands
IF the configured model provider or MCP server retains prompts or file contents outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of OpenHands inputs
Use a jurisdiction-approved model provider
Review retention settings for the configured provider
Strip identifiers before passing artifacts across the pair
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
